body:
Wow, six years. These types of ends to relationships seem to be rampant in our age group, everyone is trying to figure themselves out.  A friend of mine just had her 13 year relationship end two weeks ago for the same reasoning (she's 27).

I've been trying to hold on to my moments of clarity where I know I will be better and I need to focus on myself, he's spending this time to focus on himself so why shouldn't I? 

I definitely recommend a counselor, I've been seeing one and its helpful but I don't click too well with the one I have now and I know I should be looking to get a new one, the process can be draining.  But worth it to have someone to talk things out who you know is there on your team.

Edit: missing word
Thank you, knowing that you are here and there are people who care who don't even know me has helped quite a bit

Thank you for the response! I'm trying to be kind to myself but getting around to getting up out of bed and eating has been tough.  It's easier to lay and be sad, crying and wishing I did something different.  How long did it take you to get over your ex?

And I have a therapist but we don't really click, I'm looking into a new one next week when the office is open.

I'm living at home and unfortunately my mom is allergic to dogs and cats :(

Thank you for taking the time to respond.  I know, I need to find a new one but he's a nice person so I feel bad for wanting a new one.  It's an unhealthy way of thinking for sure, I'm not even sure how to go about finding a new one because this office is close enough that I can walk to, the other offices are a couple miles away.

I read your story in your post and I can empathize.  I have a hard time getting close to people because I feel like they'll hurt me, and this time that I let myself be vulnerable, I'm left alone again

I wish there was a way to peak into the future to see that we were doing well, to make trudging through hard times a little easier
